SCORE: interest_signature_hypball | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: interest_signature_hypball | IN_SCOPE | Training-only user-cohort transition counts define a per-item signature and parent; Poincaré tangent shift and geodesic distance affect the first-token assignment on that parent’s code subset. Behavior-off, Euclidean, and both-on switches are specified, with assignment and Stage3 outcomes observable; only the both-on run is trained.
EVIDENCE: interest_signature_hypball | E1 E2 E4 E5 E6 E8 E9 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: interest_signature_hypball | Hashing users into cohorts does not establish that the cohorts represent interests; the measured cohort-profile signal supports predecessor-cohort overlap, but not necessarily the proposed hashed-user cohorts or their connection to improved next-item recommendation. The constrained parent allocation may also strand first-level capacity.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: interest_signature_hypball | If all items have identical cohort signatures, their maximum-mass parent is identical; the behavior shift is common across items, so it need not improve their relative first-token assignments and can instead act as a shared distortion.
RATIONALE: interest_signature_hypball | behavior_evidence=4: E9 reports measured, non-degenerate cohort-profile overlap (positive 0.9291 vs negative 0.8871; overlap exceeds all ten negatives for 0.5898 of pairs), but that statistic is for predecessor cohorts, not the proposal’s hashed-user assignment, so the SID hypothesis is not fully audited. geometry_necessity=3: the curved log/exp and geodesic assignment are in the coupled pathway, but E6 records weaker results for existing geodesic-coarse variants than Euclidean L1 controls; no matched geometry argument rules out a Euclidean shift. novelty=2: the proposal differs in its user-hash signature and restricted code allocation, but E6–E7 show nearby successor-geodesic and tangent-residual mechanisms; a traceable prior-art comparison is UNKNOWN, resolvable by a bounded comparison against the cited mechanisms and ledger definitions. downstream_mechanism=4: the changed first-token assignment and intended prefix predictability are named; E6–E7 provide relevant existing prefix/beam measurements, not evidence for this proposal’s direction. falsifiability=4: the three switches are named and assignment/prefix diagnostics plus Stage3 Recall are specified, but exact matching of the off-switch controls is not fully detailed. implementability=3: the computation is specified, but allocation when parents exceed available codes and the scale/ball-boundary safeguards are unresolved; a bounded implementation audit would resolve these points. exploration_value=2: it is a variation in a family with measured nearby negative results. No Stage 3 outcome is measured here.

SCORE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | IN_SCOPE | Training-only directed successor counts produce each item’s smoothed successor distribution and embedding barycentre; Möbius translation, exponential map, and Poincaré geodesic distance use that behaviour signal to alter unrestricted first-token assignment. Behaviour-off, Euclidean, and both-on switches are specified, with assignment and Stage3 outcomes observable; only the both-on run is trained.
EVIDENCE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | E1 E2 E4 E5 E6 E7 E8 E10 E11 E12 E13
OBJECTION: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | The proposed barycentre is built from frozen item embeddings, but the bundle’s measured behavioural evidence describes successor entropy and predecessor-cohort profiles; it does not establish that embedding barycentres encode useful continuation roles. The barycentre may also be dominated by popular destinations.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | If an item has two equally weighted successors with embeddings x and −x, their weighted mean is zero; after centering, that item receives no behaviour displacement even though its successor distribution is nontrivial.
RATIONALE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | behavior_evidence=3: the training-only signal and its computation are explicit, and E5 supports heterogeneous successor predictability, but no provided observed statistic validates successor-embedding barycentres or their coverage. geometry_necessity=3: Möbius addition and geodesic assignment are computationally coupled to the barycentre; the existing geodesic and tangent variants in E6–E7 underperform Euclidean L1 controls, and the proposal does not rule out a matched Euclidean translation. novelty=2: the per-item barycentre translation differs from a discrete parent constraint, but it is close to measured successor-geodesic/tangent mechanisms in E6–E7; prior-art distinction is UNKNOWN, resolvable by a bounded comparison with those mechanisms and their definitions. downstream_mechanism=4: the first-level assignment is explicitly changed while residual input remains unshifted, and prefix predictability/identity diagnostics are named; the expected direction is a hypothesis, not a measurement. falsifiability=4: the three switches and a Stage3 threshold are specified, with assignment and prefix diagnostics, though control matching is not fully formalized. implementability=3: core operations are stated, but normalization/centering details, curvature projection and boundary safeguards need precise implementation checks; the bounded check is a numerical audit on training latents. exploration_value=2: it is a nearby variation of previously measured successor-geometric mechanisms. No Stage 3 outcome is measured here.

SCORE: transition-radial-sector-vq | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: transition-radial-sector-vq | IN_SCOPE | Training-only popularity-smoothed directed successor profiles determine item sectors and prototypes; the behavior-conditioned point is mapped to the Poincaré ball and assigned by geodesic distance within its sector. Behaviour-off, Euclidean, and both-on switches are required by the proposal’s test plan, with assignment and Stage3 outcomes observable; only the both-on run is trained.
EVIDENCE: transition-radial-sector-vq | E1 E2 E4 E5 E6 E7 E8 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: transition-radial-sector-vq | The mechanism combines successor-profile sectors with a sector prototype shift, but the bundle does not measure whether profile-based clusters align with predictive prefixes. In addition, the specified “radial” title is not reflected in a separately defined radial operation; the actual curved operation is exponential mapping plus geodesic distance.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: transition-radial-sector-vq | If all successor profiles are identical, deterministic clustering can place every item in one sector; the sector prototype then adds the same vector to every latent, leaving no item-specific behavioural distinction from that shift.
RATIONALE: transition-radial-sector-vq | behavior_evidence=3: the training-only directed signal and its computation are explicit, and E5 documents successor-entropy variation, but no observed statistic validates these KL sectors or their coverage. geometry_necessity=3: the curved mapping and geodesic assignment affect the behaviour-conditioned first-token computation, but the name “radial” adds no explicit radial operation, and E6 reports weaker existing geodesic-coarse results than Euclidean controls. novelty=2: sector-restricted assignment plus a prototype shift is distinct in combination but near measured successor-geodesic/coarse and tangent-residual mechanisms (E6–E7); prior-art traceability is UNKNOWN, resolvable by a bounded comparison against those ledger mechanisms. downstream_mechanism=4: the assignment change and intended coarse prefix/retained residual path are specified, with diagnostics named; expected improvement remains unmeasured. falsifiability=4: behaviour-off, geometry-off, and both-on are called for, and diagnostics plus a Stage3 criterion are given, though exact switch implementation/control matching is not supplied. implementability=3: profile clustering, PCA, scale, curvature and assignment are described, but details such as sparse KL handling, empty sectors and finite-ball clamping need a bounded implementation/numerical audit. exploration_value=2: it is a variation on previously measured successor-geometric/coarse mechanisms. No Stage 3 outcome is measured here.
